scope: Only add robot and seaside to published child-loader capability (src/host/loader-capabilities.ts). Prior eight (airship, radio, curiosity, ticket, take, seating, sofa, ordering) retained. Train, Till, Sudoku not added. No game, registry, menu, train, age, bridge, readiness, origin/source/nonce or sandbox changes.
method: Anonymous actual canonical HTTPS hub (https://aylas-puzzles.lovable.app) and the live registered children in headless Chromium. Real menu Play card launches (touch tap on phone/Duo/iPad emulation; keyboard Enter plus reduced motion on desktop), cold (fresh context) then cached (same context) at six sizes. No route interception, fake parent, forged messages, relaxed security flags or browser bypass; a read-only window message listener records real child events. Parent cover = role=status children of the session main; topmost element at viewport centre must be the visible iframe. Child loader timing is from the child's own visible loader text (Robot: 'Pip is warming up the route…'/'All parcels loaded!'; Seaside: 'Rabbit is opening the kiosk…'), sampled about every 150-300 ms.

publication.shaLimitation: Public sourceVersion remains inherited 50b7764, not the Git SHA. The new public build ID plus canonical Robot/Seaside launches with zero hub cover (the previous source drew the cover for these two; not re-observed live this turn) establish rollout, not the exact deployed SHA.

regressions.vitest: 14 files, 109 tests passed (host-session-shell: all 10 approved games stay unready with no duplicate starting cover, then 20 s slow timeout shows Try again / All games and retry; trains, money-change, sudoku keep the normal hub startup cover; pre-ready Next refused; release-freshness replacement; nextError retry; forged/hidden Back ignored).

limitations: Robot sends its real ready message about 1-2.5 s after launch while its own loader keeps painting for about 12-16 s; in cached runs ready can arrive before the first loader screenshot, so some Robot loader screenshots are after ready. This child-owned timing was recorded, not changed.
Robot was not won: solving requires programming a route and no safe, non-guessing play script was attempted. Robot Next was taken from the child's real 'Next adventure' control after Start delivery.

Seaside wins were played from the visible question and the on-screen queue order relative to the flag described by the child's own accessible scene label; feedback 'You got it right!' then the child's 'Next puzzle' control.
After Next, the promoted prepared iframe sometimes still shows its own loader (Seaside library-story fallback text or Robot 'warming up' near 95%); the hub draws no cover over it.
The 20-second slow timeout was verified by regression tests, not by a stuck live child.
Headless Chromium emulation only; not physical iPad/Safari, and no audio listening.
